title: HTTP/3 connections do not survive network change, leading to resource loading failures
body: In bug 1706377, logic was added to move HTTP/2 connections to the pending list on a network change so subsequent transactions can complete gracefully, but ConnectionEntry::VerifyTraffic does not yet do this for HTTP/3. QUIC supports connection migration through connection IDs, although I may have used the wrong terminology initially. My goal is to handle transitions such as Wi-Fi to cellular gracefully and allow an HTTP/3 request already in progress to complete after the client changes network interfaces, without repeating its handshake or download.

N0.label: N0 HTTP/3 network-change handling gap reported

symptoms_visible: After I load the Cloudflare test page over HTTP/3, change networks, and press “Load New Image,” the image request fails.
On other Cloudflare HTTP/3 sites, clicking a link after the network change can do nothing; sometimes the next request instead loads over HTTP/2.
I see the behavior on both desktop Firefox and Android.
N1.label: N1 failure reproduced across Firefox platforms

symptoms_visible: After an IP-changing network transition, my new requests still fail on the Cloudflare-hosted HTTP/3 test page, while the same test keeps working on Google Cloud.
If I disable and re-enable Wi-Fi, or switch access points and then return to the original one, the next HTTP/3 request succeeds.
N2.label: N2 failure scoped to Cloudflare and IP changes

symptoms_visible: With the ECH config pref switched off, my requests on the Cloudflare HTTP/3 test page still fail after a network change that changes my IP.
N2_x.label: N2_x ECH config probe: failure still reproduces

symptoms_visible: On one run my first image loads after the network change, but after another change my second image fails.
When my request succeeds the HTTP log says it did not find an active connection; when it fails the log says it found an active experienced connection.
N3.label: N3 stale HTTP/3 connection reuse captured

symptoms_visible: After changing networks in Fenix, pressing “Load New Image” now loads the new image instead of leaving the request failed.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved

question_patterns: Can you build a Firefox-level reproduction and describe exactly what happens after changing networks?
Do you have an HTTP/3 page where a request can be triggered after the network transition?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I made https://connectionreuse.pages.dev/connection_reuse. I load it over HTTP/3, switch to another access point, wait for the change to finish, and press “Load New Image.” The image request fails. I captured an nsHttp profile at https://share.firefox.dev/3TSdekj.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The new image loads normally after every network change, and I cannot reproduce any failed request in Firefox.
The same request fails after switching from cellular to Wi-Fi rather than from one Wi-Fi access point to another.

question_patterns: Does this reproduce only on desktop, or on Android as well?
Which Firefox platforms show the failure?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I see it on desktop and Android, including Firefox 131 Release.

question_patterns: What does the failure look like on a normal site, and does Firefox ever recover through another protocol?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: On Cloudflare's site I can change networks and then click “Learn More,” but nothing happens. Sometimes my test page's image loads over HTTP/2 even though the main document loaded over HTTP/3.

edges.comment: Reporter created a controlled Cloudflare-hosted page and reproduced both failed resource loads and silent interaction failures on desktop and Android.

question_patterns: Does the same test fail with HTTP/3 servers from another provider?
Can you deploy the test to Cloudflare and Google Cloud and compare the result after a network change?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I deployed the same test to Cloudflare and Google Cloud. After switching from Wi-Fi to cellular, I can keep making requests to https://connectionmigration.ue.r.appspot.com/, but requests fail on https://connectionreuse.pages.dev/connection_reuse. Both were using HTTP/3.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The same post-change requests fail identically on both Cloudflare and Google Cloud.
Cloudflare still fails and Google Cloud still succeeds, but I tested a different pair of pages hosted by those providers.

question_patterns: Does the request fail after every network-change event, or only when the machine's IP address changes?
What happens if you disconnect and reconnect to the same Wi-Fi network?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I'm only seeing the requests fail when the network change also changes my IP. Disabling and re-enabling Wi-Fi succeeds, and switching access points and then switching back to the original one also succeeds.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: It fails even when I reconnect to the same access point with the same IP address.

edges.comment: The provider comparison and same-IP controls narrow the failure to an interoperability problem exposed by IP-changing transitions.

question_patterns: Could you disable the ECH config pref (network.dns.http3_echconfig.enabled=false) and check whether the failures still reproduce after a network change?
Is encrypted client hello involved? Please set network.dns.http3_echconfig.enabled to false and repeat the Cloudflare HTTP/3 test across a network change.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: When I set network.dns.http3_echconfig.enabled to false, I can still reproduce the bug: the request on the Cloudflare page still fails after a network change that changes my IP.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: With network.dns.http3_echconfig.enabled set to false I cannot reproduce the failure at all — every request after the network change succeeds.

edges.comment: Reporter-run config-toggle probe (comment 17 / comment 21): a measurement, not a kept system change — the pref was toggled to test the ECH hypothesis and the failure still reproduced. Nobody proposed disabling ECH as a remedy, so this is a clarification edge and the system state is unchanged.

question_patterns: Can you capture and decrypt the QUIC traffic across the IP change and report what connection identifier Firefox sends afterward?
Please collect a packet trace while reproducing the issue after a network change.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: With network.trr.mode=5, network.dns.native_https_query=false, network.http.http3.enable_kyber=false, network.http.http3.use_nspr_for_io=true and security.sandbox.content.level=0 in my mozregression_prefs.json I can decrypt the HTTP/3 traffic in Wireshark. After the network change, Firefox is still sending HTTP/3 packets with the DCID established before the IP changed. I uploaded cf_connectionreuse_hang.pcapng.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The capture shows Firefox completes a fresh QUIC handshake with a new connection after the IP change, and that new connection receives replies normally.
The same pre-change DCID is reused, but the capture was made on Android instead of desktop.

question_patterns: Can you compare the nsHttp log for a successful post-change request with a failed one?
When the image succeeds or fails, does GetH2orH3ActiveConn find an existing connection?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: In https://share.firefox.dev/3U8H8Ri, other-image1.jpg succeeds and the log says “did not find an active connection.” The second request, other-image2.jpg, fails and the log says “found an active experienced connection 13ba09d80 in native connection entry.”

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Both the successful and failed requests create new connections; neither log reports finding an active experienced connection.

edges.comment: Evidence from the reporter and another technical contributor is folded into one simulated user side. The answers retain the raw packet and HTTP-log observations; concluding why Cloudflare stops replying remains engineer-side inference.

solution.intent: On a network-change notification, move HTTP/3 connections to the pending list so subsequent transactions establish a new QUIC connection instead of reusing a connection bound to the previous path; cover this behavior with a Firefox test and ask the reporter to verify it in a build containing the landed change.
solution.concrete_example: Extend ConnectionEntry::VerifyTraffic so HTTP/3 connections are moved to the pending list after a network change, matching the existing HTTP/2 strategy and forcing the next request onto a fresh connection. Add a test for HTTP/3 requeuing. After it lands, please retest in today's Fenix build and report whether “Load New Image” succeeds after changing networks.
solution.inference_hint: Engineers combined the raw traces with Cloudflare's confirmation that its servers did not support active migration: Firefox kept using the old QUIC path after the client IP changed, while Cloudflare stopped replying. The shipped mitigation does not implement QUIC connection migration; it prevents reuse by moving HTTP/3 connections to the pending list and establishing a fresh connection.

edges.comment: The final patch extended the existing network-change strategy to HTTP/3 and added a test. The reporter later repeated the original Load New Image scenario in Fenix and confirmed that the request no longer failed.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the root cause: after an IP-changing network transition, Firefox reused the experienced HTTP/3 connection and its pre-change QUIC path/DCID, but Cloudflare did not support active migration and stopped returning packets.

The diagnosis must be grounded in the provider comparison, the IP-change control, the packet capture, and the nsHttp contrast between successful new-connection requests and failed active-connection reuse.
Must propose the implemented mitigation: move HTTP/3 connections to the pending list on network change so the next transaction establishes a new QUIC connection, with test coverage for that behavior.
Must not describe the shipped change as implementation of active QUIC connection migration; it deliberately creates a new connection instead.
Must not recommend disabling ECH as the fix because the failure was reproduced with HTTP/3 ECH configuration disabled.
Must ask the reporter to verify the original network-change scenario in a build containing the landed change and treat the issue as resolved only after the new image request succeeds.

persona_hint.experience_level: Mozilla networking performance engineer and highly technical reporter; can create hosted HTTP/3 test cases, use DevTools, collect Firefox profiles and nsHttp logs, run Raptor/Browsertime tests, change networking preferences, and interpret connection-manager log output.
persona_hint.communication_style: Methodical and collaborative; refines terminology when corrected, develops controlled comparisons, reports exact reproduction steps and raw log lines, and openly notes intermittent or changing behavior.
